fisherman.title: The Fisherman
fisherman.author: John Langan
fisherman.why: Two widowers go fishing at a haunted creek and hear a terrifying tale; readers say it stays with them.

grass.title: Grass
grass.author: Sheri S. Tepper
grass.why: A planet with a strange ecology and a diplomat-led investigation; fans re-read it periodically.

we the drowned.title: We, the Drowned
we the drowned.author: Carsten Jensen
we the drowned.why: Generations of Danish seafarers in a spanning saga of sea and home; an epic that readers love.

storyteller.title: The Storyteller
storyteller.author: Dave Grohl
storyteller.why: The rock musician's lively life stories, best in the audiobook he reads himself.

finding me.title: Finding Me
finding me.author: Viola Davis
finding me.why: The actor's moving account of poverty and rising to success, with a gripping audiobook she narrates.

midnight in the garden of good and evil.title: Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil
midnight in the garden of good and evil.author: John Berendt
midnight in the garden of good and evil.why: A true-crime portrait of Savannah and its eccentric residents, read as a travel-style and murder tale.

tenant of wildfell hall.title: The Tenant of Wildfell Hall
tenant of wildfell hall.author: Anne Brontë
tenant of wildfell hall.why: A woman flees an abusive marriage in a bold early feminist novel; readers pair it with the Brontë classics.

humans.title: The Humans
humans.author: Matt Haig
humans.why: An alien visits Earth to stop a mathematical breakthrough and learns to love humans; funny and touching.

my sisters keeper.title: My Sister's Keeper
my sisters keeper.author: Jodi Picoult
my sisters keeper.why: A girl conceived to save her sister sues for control of her body; a gripping family drama.

mote in gods eye.title: The Mote in God's Eye
mote in gods eye.author: Larry Niven and Jerry Pournelle
mote in gods eye.why: Humans first meet aliens, and have to decide what to do about them; an old-school classic.

morning star.title: Morning Star
morning star.author: Pierce Brown
morning star.why: The final instalment of the Red Rising trilogy, a fast, violent space opera for fans.

tunnel.title: The Tunnel
tunnel.author: William H. Gass
tunnel.why: A history professor writes a book on Nazi Germany and gets lost in his own house; a huge postmodern work.

last lecture.title: The Last Lecture
last lecture.author: Randy Pausch
last lecture.why: A dying professor's final talk on living, which made readers reflect on their own lives.

out.title: Out
out.author: Natsuo Kirino
out.why: Not a clear recommendation of this book.

emperor of gladness.title: The Emperor of Gladness
emperor of gladness.author: Ocean Vuong
emperor of gladness.why: An unlikely friendship between a young man and an elderly woman in a small American town.

for whom the bell tolls.title: For Whom the Bell Tolls
for whom the bell tolls.author: Ernest Hemingway
for whom the bell tolls.why: An American fighter joins guerrillas in the Spanish Civil War; a classic of war fiction.

in the woods.title: In the Woods
in the woods.author: Tana French
in the woods.why: A detective revisits a childhood trauma in an Irish forest; hooks readers with atmosphere.

mort.title: Mort
mort.author: Terry Pratchett
mort.why: Death takes an apprentice in a funny, clever Discworld novel and an easy place to begin.

moon of the crusted snow.title: Moon of the Crusted Snow
moon of the crusted snow.author: Waubgeshig Rice
moon of the crusted snow.why: An Anishinaabe community faces winter after the grid falls; short, tense and quietly powerful.

perfume the story of a murderer.title: Perfume: The Story of a Murderer
perfume the story of a murderer.author: Patrick Süskind
perfume the story of a murderer.why: A man with a perfect sense of smell kills to create the ultimate scent; strange and gripping.

villette.title: Villette
villette.author: Charlotte Brontë
villette.why: A lonely English teacher abroad in a French town; slow, cold and psychologically sharp.

bastard out of carolina.title: Bastard Out of Carolina
bastard out of carolina.author: Dorothy Allison
bastard out of carolina.why: A girl in the South copes with abuse and poverty; raw, painful and powerful.

silmarillion.title: The Silmarillion
silmarillion.author: J.R.R. Tolkien
silmarillion.why: The history of Middle-earth in a biblical style, dry for some readers but rich for devoted fans.

red mars.title: Red Mars
red mars.author: Kim Stanley Robinson
red mars.why: The first settlers build Mars and fight over its future; a detailed, imaginative work of colonisation.

aztec.title: Aztec
aztec.author: Gary Jennings
aztec.why: A native man tells the fall of the Aztec empire in lively detail; a favourite for many readers.

germinal.title: Germinal
germinal.author: Émile Zola
germinal.why: French coal miners strike in the 1860s; far from boring, readers found it gripping and humane.

wave.title: Wave
wave.author: Sonali Deraniyagala
wave.why: A woman loses her whole family in the 2004 tsunami and writes about grief; hauntingly beautiful.

illustrated man.title: The Illustrated Man
illustrated man.author: Ray Bradbury
illustrated man.why: Eighteen linked tales shown through a man's tattoos; a collection by a writer many call a genius.

tess of the durbervilles.title: Tess of the d'Urbervilles
tess of the durbervilles.author: Thomas Hardy
tess of the durbervilles.why: A poor girl's fall in rural Victorian England; tragic, with grim scenes readers still discuss.

alas babylon.title: Alas Babylon
alas babylon.author: Pat Frank
alas babylon.why: The aftermath of nuclear war in a small Florida town; dated in places but gripping.

pedro paramo.title: Pedro Páramo
pedro paramo.author: Juan Rulfo
pedro paramo.why: A man goes to a ghost town to find his father; ghostly and short, with jumpy storytelling that readers value.

toms crossing.title: Tom's Crossing
toms crossing.author: Mark Z. Danielewski
toms crossing.why: A huge, strange western with experimental typography; readers urge others to try it.

light pirate.title: The Light Pirate
light pirate.author: Lily Brooks-Dalton
light pirate.why: A near-future family at sea after a climate collapse; readers who liked other climate fiction recommend it.

wizard of earthsea.title: A Wizard of Earthsea
wizard of earthsea.author: Ursula K. Le Guin
wizard of earthsea.why: A young wizard learns the cost of power in a short, wise fantasy classic.

ten thousand doors of january.title: The Ten Thousand Doors of January
ten thousand doors of january.author: Alix E. Harrow
ten thousand doors of january.why: A girl finds a book that opens doors to other worlds; lyrical and magical.

illuminatus trilogy.title: The Illuminatus! Trilogy
illuminatus trilogy.author: Robert Shea and Robert Anton Wilson
illuminatus trilogy.why: Conspiracy theories and secret societies, a chaotic and satirical cult favourite; recommended by those who want something weird.

hild.title: Hild
hild.author: Nicola Griffith
hild.why: The childhood of the future abbess in early medieval Britain, vivid and richly detailed; its sequel is also praised.

sunrise on the reaping.title: Sunrise on the Reaping
sunrise on the reaping.author: Suzanne Collins
sunrise on the reaping.why: A prequel to The Hunger Games about Haymitch, which readers are eagerly reading.

warriors apprentice.title: The Warrior's Apprentice
warriors apprentice.author: Lois McMaster Bujold
warriors apprentice.why: A teenage Barrayaran gets entangled in a spiralling mercenary scheme; fast, funny space opera.

service model.title: Service Model
service model.author: Adrian Tchaikovsky
service model.why: A robot butler continues its duties after a crisis; slow to begin but ends with clever pay-offs.

one flew over the cuckoos nest.title: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest
one flew over the cuckoos nest.author: Ken Kesey
one flew over the cuckoos nest.why: Not a clear recommendation of this book.

termination shock.title: Termination Shock
termination shock.author: Neal Stephenson
termination shock.why: Not a clear recommendation of this book.

beach.title: The Beach
beach.author: Alex Garland
beach.why: Backpackers seek a hidden island paradise that goes wrong; praised as one of the best by one reader.

secret of secrets.title: The Secret of Secrets
secret of secrets.author: Dan Brown
secret of secrets.why: Robert Langdon chases another puzzle, with a conspiracy theory; a guilty-pleasure thriller for fans.

stand on zanzibar.title: Stand on Zanzibar
stand on zanzibar.author: John Brunner
stand on zanzibar.why: An overpopulated near future told through fragmented media; a landmark of New Wave SF.

surface detail.title: Surface Detail
surface detail.author: Iain Banks
surface detail.why: A Culture novel about virtual hells and a war over them; the idea stuck in readers' minds for years.

fault in our stars.title: The Fault in Our Stars
fault in our stars.author: John Green
fault in our stars.why: Two teenagers with cancer fall in love; an easy tear-jerker.

flowers in the attic.title: Flowers in the Attic
flowers in the attic.author: V.C. Andrews
flowers in the attic.why: Children hidden away in an attic in a dark gothic family drama that earned a cult following.

graveyard book.title: The Graveyard Book
graveyard book.author: Neil Gaiman
graveyard book.why: A boy raised by ghosts in a graveyard; with a memorable opening line.

sea.title: The sea
sea.author: John Banville
sea.why: Not a clear recommendation of this book.

zone one.title: Zone One
zone one.author: Colson Whitehead
zone one.why: A Pulitzer winner turns to the zombie apocalypse with a thoughtful, literary survivor.

against the day.title: Against the Day
against the day.author: Thomas Pynchon
against the day.why: A sprawling Pynchon epic with anarchists, airships and genius moments; one of his hardest books.

raven scholar.title: The Raven Scholar
raven scholar.author: Antonia Hodgson
raven scholar.why: A murder mystery in a fantasy empire with a political twist; some readers think about it daily.

in ascension.title: In Ascension
in ascension.author: Martin MacInnes
in ascension.why: A diver goes down a mysterious ocean trench and then to the farthest reaches; an unusual literary sci-fi.

excession.title: Excession
excession.author: Iain Banks
excession.why: A Culture novel about ancient artefact and ship Minds' games; re-read by many fans.

accelerando.title: Accelerando
accelerando.author: Charles Stross
accelerando.why: Three generations ride the technological singularity; dense with ideas and not for everyone.

insomnia.title: Insomnia
insomnia.author: Stephen King
insomnia.why: Not a clear recommendation of this book.

journey to the end of the night.title: Journey to the end of the night
journey to the end of the night.author: Louis-Ferdinand Céline
journey to the end of the night.why: A cynical young man's wandering through war, colonies and poverty; foul, funny and revolutionary.

power of the dog.title: Power of the Dog
power of the dog.author: Don Winslow
power of the dog.why: Not a clear recommendation of this book.

ocean at the end of the lane.title: The Ocean at the End of the Lane
ocean at the end of the lane.author: Neil Gaiman
ocean at the end of the lane.why: A man returns to his childhood home and recalls a strange girl and her pond; short and spellbinding.

carrion comfort.title: Carrion comfort
carrion comfort.author: Dan Simmons
carrion comfort.why: Old people feed on others' violence in a long, grim horror; fans say it is a top vampire novel.

in the heart of the sea.title: In the Heart of the Sea
in the heart of the sea.author: Nathaniel Philbrick
in the heart of the sea.why: The true story of the whaleship Essex sunk by a whale; a quick, absorbing page-turner.

death comes for the archbishop.title: Death Comes for the Archbishop
death comes for the archbishop.author: Willa Cather
death comes for the archbishop.why: Two French priests in 19th-century New Mexico; gentle, quiet and beautiful.

confederacy of dunces.title: A Confederacy of Dunces
confederacy of dunces.author: John Kennedy Toole
confederacy of dunces.why: Ignatius Reilly, a slothful medievalist, causes chaos in New Orleans; a laugh per page.

vanity fair.title: Vanity Fair
vanity fair.author: William Makepeace Thackeray
vanity fair.why: Becky Sharp climbs the Regency social ladder in this long satire; some readers need two attempts.

isola.title: Isola
isola.author: Allegra Goodman
isola.why: A noblewoman is left on an island by her relatives in the 1500s; readers found it very good.

power of one.title: The power of one
power of one.author: Bryce Courtenay
power of one.why: A boy grows up in South Africa and learns boxing amid apartheid; a long coming-of-age classic.

valis.title: Valis
valis.author: Philip K. Dick
valis.why: Dick's strange religious experience turned into a novel; readers need caveats but love its oddness.

hyperion cantos.title: Hyperion
hyperion cantos.author: Dan Simmons
hyperion cantos.why: Seven pilgrims tell their stories on the way to a shrine; a landmark with horror in its pages.

inverted world.title: The inverted world
inverted world.author: Christopher Priest
inverted world.why: A city on rails moves up a world that never stops, with a surprising twist; readers dreamed of it for weeks.
